title.zh: 卷二十五 列傳第十九: 裴忌 孫瑒
title.raw: 卷二十五 列傳第十九: 裴忌 孫瑒 Volume 25: Pei Ji; Sun Yang

sentences.zh: 忌少聰敏，有識量，頗涉史傳，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Ji in youth was clever and keen, had judgment and capacity, had read widely in histories and annals, and was praised by men of the day.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Ji was quick and perceptive, with sound judgment; he had dipped deep into histories and won praise in his day.

sentences.zh: 解褐梁豫章王法曹參軍。

translations.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as law officer in the establishment of Liang's Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His first post was law officer on the staff of Liang's Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，忌招集勇力，隨高祖征討，累功為寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Ji gathered bold fighters, followed the Founder on campaigns, and by accumulated merit was made Pacifying-Distance General.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled Ji raised fighting men and marched with the Founder. Merit piled up until he was made pacifying-distance general.

sentences.zh: 及高祖誅王僧辯，僧辯弟僧智舉兵據吳郡，高祖遣黃他率眾攻之，僧智出兵於西昌門拒戰，他與相持，不能克。

translations.literal: When the Founder executed Wang Sengbian, Sengbian's younger brother Sengzhi raised troops and held Wu commandery; the Founder sent Huang Ta at the head of the host to attack him; Sengzhi led troops out at the Xichang Gate to resist; Ta locked with him and could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founder killed Wang Sengbian, Sengbian's brother Sengzhi seized Wu commandery. The Founder sent Huang Ta with an army against him. Sengzhi marched out the Xichang Gate to fight. Ta held him at bay and could not break him.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂忌曰：「三吳奧壤，舊稱饒沃，雖凶荒之餘，猶為殷盛，而今賊徒扇聚，天下搖心，非公無以定之，宜善思其策。

translations.literal: The Founder said to Ji: "The Three Wu are a vital land, of old called rich and fertile; though in the wake of famine and ruin they remain abundant and thriving, yet now the rebels gather and sway the hearts of the realm—without you they cannot be settled. You should think well on your plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder told Ji: "The Three Wu are the empire's rich core. Even after famine they stay prosperous, yet rebels now gather and the realm wavers. No one but you can settle this. Think hard on your plan.

sentences.zh: 」忌乃勒部下精兵，輕行倍道，自錢塘直趣吳郡，〔一〕夜至城下，鼓譟薄之。

translations.literal: " Ji then mustered picked troops of his command, marched light and by double stages, went straight from Qiantang toward Wu commandery, Editorial footnote marker 1. and in one night reached below the walls, beat drums, clamored, and pressed the assault.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji mustered his best troops, traveled light at forced march from Qiantang straight for Wu commandery, [1] and in a single night was under the walls beating drums and storming the gate.

sentences.zh: 僧智疑大軍至，輕舟奔杜龕，忌入據其郡。

translations.literal: Sengzhi suspected a great army had come, fled in a light boat to Du Kan, and Ji entered and held the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhi thought a great host had arrived, fled by light boat to Du Kan, and Ji entered and took the commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，表授吳郡太守。

translations.literal: The Founder commended him and memorialized him appointed Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder praised him and memorialized his appointment as administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，徵為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Ji was summoned as Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne Ji was summoned as left guard general.

sentences.zh: 天嘉初，出為持節、南康內史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he went out as Bearer of the Staff and Interior Minister of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tiancheng (560) he was sent out as bearer of the staff and interior minister of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 時義安太守張紹賓據郡反，世祖以忌為持節、都督嶺北諸軍事，率眾討平之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Shaobin, Administrator of Yian, held the commandery in rebellion; Emperor Wen made Ji Bearer of the Staff and Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the North of the Range, and he led the host to campaign and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shaobin, administrator of Yian, rebelled and held his commandery. Emperor Wen made Ji bearer of the staff and commander of the armies north of the range, and he led troops to crush him.

sentences.zh: 還除散騎常侍、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: On his return he was removed and made Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Left Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and left chief clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，授雲麾將軍、衛尉卿，封東興縣侯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given Cloud-Banner General and Chamberlain for the Palace, enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing county with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made cloud-banner general and chamberlain for the palace, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing with six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及華皎稱兵上流，高宗時為錄尚書輔政，盡命眾軍出討，委忌總知中外城防諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Hua Jiao raised troops upriver, Emperor Xuan was then Recorder of the Secretariat assisting in government; he ordered all armies out to campaign and entrusted Ji with overall command of inner and outer city defense and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao rebelled upriver, Emperor Xuan was regent as recorder of the Secretariat. He sent every army against Jiao and put Ji in charge of all city defenses, within and without.

sentences.zh: 及皎平，高宗即位，太建元年，授東陽太守，改封樂安縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Emperor Xuan took the throne; in the first year of Taijian he was given Administrator of Dongyang, changed in enfeoffment to Marquis of Le'an county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiao fell, Emperor Xuan succeeded. In Taijian year 1 (569) Ji was made administrator of Dongyang and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Le'an with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為太府卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered office as Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he entered court as grand steward.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉都官尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 吳明徹督眾軍北伐，詔忌以本官監明徹軍。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche commanded the armies on the northern campaign; an edict ordered Ji in his present office to oversee Mingche's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche led the northern campaign. An edict made Ji, in his existing post, overseer of Mingche's army.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，授軍師將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified he was given Army Master General and Inspector of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified he was made army-master general and inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 忌善於綏撫，甚得民和。

translations.literal: Ji was skilled at soothing and gathering; he won the people's harmony exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was skilled at winning people over and enjoyed deep goodwill among them.

sentences.zh: 改授使持節、都督譙州諸軍事、譙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was reassigned Bearer of the Staff and Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Qiao province and Inspector of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned bearer of the staff, commander of Qiao province, and inspector of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 未及之官，會明徹受詔進討彭、汴，以忌為都督，與明徹掎角俱進。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, Mingche received orders to advance and campaign against Peng and Bian; Ji was made commander and advanced with Mingche in pincer.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up office, Mingche was ordered to strike Peng and Bian. Ji was made commander and marched in pincer with him.

sentences.zh: 呂梁軍敗，陷于周，周授上開府。

translations.literal: The army was defeated at Lüliang and fell into Zhou; Zhou made him Senior Opening General.
translations.idiomatic: The army was broken at Lüliang and he fell into Zhou hands. Zhou made him senior opening general.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十四年卒於長安，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Sui's Kaihuang era he died at Chang'an, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 14 of Sui (594) he died at Chang'an, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 孫瑒字德璉，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Sun Yang, styled Delian, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yang, styled Delian, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖文惠，齊越騎校尉、清遠太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wenhui was Qi Colonel of the Yue Cavalry and Administrator of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wenhui had been Qi colonel of the Yue cavalry and administrator of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 父循道，〔二〕梁中散大夫，以雅素知名。

translations.literal: His father Xundao, Editorial footnote marker 2. was Liang Palace Attendant and was famed for refined simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xundao [2] was a Liang palace attendant, known for refined simplicity.

sentences.zh: 瑒少倜儻，好謀略，博涉經史，尤便書翰。

translations.literal: Yang in youth was free and bold, loved strategy, read widely in the classics and histories, and was especially skilled at letters.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yang was bold and fond of strategy; he read widely in the classics and histories and excelled at correspondence.

sentences.zh: 起家梁輕車臨川嗣王行參軍，累遷為安西邵陵王水曹中兵參軍事。

translations.literal: He began his career as acting aide in the light-chariot service of Liang's Heir of Linchuan, and was promoted in succession to water-and-arms clerk in the military staff of the Prince of Shao-ling, Pacifier of the West.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as acting aide to Liang's Heir of Linchuan in the light-chariot office, then rose to water-and-arms clerk on the military staff of the Prince of Shao-ling, pacifier of the west.

sentences.zh: 王出鎮郢州，瑒盡室隨府，甚被賞遇。

translations.literal: When the prince went out to garrison Yingzhou, Yang moved his whole household with the headquarters and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took up his post at Yingzhou, Yang brought his whole household to the headquarters and won high favor.

sentences.zh: 太清之難，授假節、宣猛將軍、軍主。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of Taiping he was given acting staff, made Fierce Martial General, and made army commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiping turmoil he received acting credentials as fierce-martial general and army commander.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯之討侯景也，王琳為前軍，琳與瑒同門，乃表薦為戎昭將軍、宜都太守，仍從僧辯救徐文盛於武昌。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian campaigned against Hou Jing, Wang Lin was vanguard; Lin and Yang were of the same gate, and Lin memorialized recommending him as Martial-Announcements General and Administrator of Yidu, and he followed Sengbian to rescue Xu Wensheng at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian attacked Hou Jing, Wang Lin led the van. Lin and Yang were schoolmates; Lin recommended him as martial-announcements general and administrator of Yidu, and he followed Sengbian to relieve Xu Wensheng at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 會郢州陷，乃留軍鎮巴陵，脩戰守之備。

translations.literal: When Yingzhou fell he remained with the army to garrison Baling and repaired preparations for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzhou fell he stayed behind to hold Baling and strengthened its defenses.

sentences.zh: 俄而侯景兵至，日夜攻圍，瑒督所部兵悉力拒戰，賊眾奔退。

translations.literal: Soon Hou Jing's troops arrived and attacked day and night; Yang supervised his command in full strength to resist; the rebel host broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hou Jing's troops came and besieged him day and night. Yang led his men in a full defense and drove the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 瑒從大軍沿流而下，及克姑熟，瑒力戰有功，除員外散騎常侍，封富陽縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Yang followed the great army downriver; when Guni was taken Yang fought hard with merit; he was removed and made Supernumerary Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, enfeoffed Marquis of Fuyang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main fleet downstream. At the taking of Guni he fought with distinction and was made supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and Marquis of Fuyang with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋授假節、雄信將軍、衡陽內史，未及之官，仍遷衡州平南府司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was given acting staff, made Trustworthy Faith General and Interior Minister of Hengyang; before he could take up the post he was transferred to marshal of the Pacify-the-South headquarters in Heng province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received acting staff as trustworthy-faith general and interior minister of Hengyang. Before he took office he was made marshal of the pacify-the-south headquarters in Heng province.

sentences.zh: 破黃洞蠻賊有功，除東莞太守，行廣州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit in breaking the Yellow-Cave Man rebels he was removed and made Administrator of Dongguan, acting Administrator of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For breaking the Yellow-Cave rebels he was made administrator of Dongguan and acting administrator of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋除智武將軍，監湘州事。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made Intelligent Martial General and overseer of Xiang province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made intelligent-martial general and overseer of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 敬帝嗣位，授持節、仁威將軍、巴州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Honored Emperor succeeded he was given staff, made Benevolent Prestige General, and Administrator of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: When the Honored Emperor succeeded he received the staff as benevolent-prestige general and administrator of Ba.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，王琳立梁永嘉王蕭莊於郢州，徵瑒為太府卿，〔三〕加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Wang Lin set up Liang's Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang at Yingzhou; Yang was summoned as Grand Steward, Editorial footnote marker 3. and promoted to Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Wang Lin enthroned Liang's Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang at Yingzhou. Yang was summoned as grand steward [3] and promoted to direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 及王琳入寇，以瑒為使持節、散騎常侍、都督郢荊巴武湘五州諸軍事、安西將軍、郢州刺史，總留府之任。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin invaded, Yang was made Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in the five provinces of Ying, Jing, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, Pacifying-the-West General, and Inspector of Ying, with overall charge of the rear headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin invaded, Yang was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of Ying, Jing, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, pacifying-the-west general and inspector of Ying, with full charge of the rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 周遣大將史寧率眾四萬，乘虛奄至，瑒助防張世〔貴〕舉外城以應之〔四〕，所失軍民男女三千餘口。

translations.literal: Zhou sent the great general Shi Ning at the head of forty thousand men, who came by surprise in force; Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shi [Gui] raised the outer city to welcome them, Editorial footnote marker 4. and there were lost among soldiers and people, men and women, more than three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent the great general Shi Ning with forty thousand men in a sudden rush. Yang's assistant defender Zhang Shi [Gui] opened the outer city to them. [4] More than three thousand soldiers and civilians, men and women, were lost.

sentences.zh: 周軍又起土山高梯，日夜攻逼，因風縱火，燒其內城南面五十餘樓。

translations.literal: The Zhou army again raised earthen hills and high ladders and attacked day and night; they took advantage of the wind to set fire and burned more than fifty towers on the inner city's south face.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army raised siege mounds and scaling ladders and pressed day and night. They used the wind to fire the inner city's southern face and burned more than fifty towers.

sentences.zh: 時瑒兵不滿千人，乘城拒守，瑒親自撫巡，行酒賦食，士卒皆為之用命。

translations.literal: At that time Yang's troops were fewer than a thousand; he manned the walls to resist; Yang personally went about encouraging them, walking the ramparts with wine and food; the soldiers all fought to the death for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had fewer than a thousand men. He held the walls himself, walking the battlements with wine and food. Every soldier fought for him to the last.

sentences.zh: 周人苦攻不能克，乃矯授瑒柱國、郢州刺史，封萬戶郡公。

translations.literal: The Zhou men attacked bitterly and could not overcome him; they then falsely invested him as Pillar of State, Inspector of Ying, and Duke of a Ten-Thousand-Household Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou attacked hard and failed. They then falsely invested him as pillar of state, inspector of Ying, and duke of a ten-thousand-household commandery.

sentences.zh: 瑒偽許以緩之，而潛修戰具，樓雉器械，一朝嚴設，周人甚憚焉。

translations.literal: Yang pretended to agree to gain time, while secretly repairing war gear; towers, parapets, and engines were in one morning set in strict array; the Zhou men greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang feigned acceptance to buy time while secretly readying arms. Towers, parapets, and engines stood complete by morning, and the Zhou were deeply afraid.

sentences.zh: 及聞大軍敗王琳，乘勝而進，周兵乃解。

translations.literal: When he heard the great army had defeated Wang Lin and was advancing in victory, the Zhou troops then lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the main army had broken Wang Lin and was marching in triumph, the Zhou lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 瑒於是盡有中流之地，集其將士而謂之曰：「吾與王公陳力協義，同獎梁室，亦已勤矣。

translations.literal: Yang then held all the midstream lands; he gathered his generals and said to them: "I and the princes exerted strength together in righteousness and jointly upheld the house of Liang—we have already toiled enough.
translations.idiomatic: Yang then held the entire mid-Yangzi. He assembled his officers and said: "We served the princes in righteousness and upheld Liang together. We have labored long enough.

sentences.zh: 今時事如此，天可違乎！

translations.literal: Now the times are thus—can Heaven be defied!
translations.idiomatic: The times stand as they do. Who defies Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」遂遣使奉表詣闕。

translations.literal: " He then sent envoys with a memorial to the court.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent envoys with a memorial to court.

sentences.zh: 天嘉元年，授使持節、散騎常侍、安南將軍、湘州刺史，封定襄縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was given Bearer of the Staff, Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Pacifying-the-South General, and Inspector of Xiang, enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 1 (560) he was made bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry regular attendant, pacifying-the-south general and inspector of Xiang, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dingxiang with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 瑒懷不自安，乃固請入朝，徵為散騎常侍、中領軍。

translations.literal: Yang was uneasy at heart and firmly asked to enter court; he was summoned as Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yang could not rest easy and begged to come to court. He was summoned as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and central army commander.

sentences.zh: 〔五〕未拜，而世祖從容謂瑒曰：「昔朱買臣願為本郡，卿豈有意乎？

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 5. Before he took the appointment, Emperor Wen spoke to Yang at ease and said: "Of old Zhu Maichen wished to be magistrate of his home commandery—do you have such a wish?
translations.idiomatic: [5] Before he took office, Emperor Wen said to him gently: "Zhu Maichen once longed to govern his home commandery. Do you feel the same?

sentences.zh: 」仍改授持節、安東將軍、吳郡太守，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon reassigned Bearer of the Staff, Pacifying-the-East General, and Administrator of Wu commandery, and given one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then made bearer of the staff, pacifying-the-east general, and administrator of Wu commandery, with a suite of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 及將之鎮，乘輿幸近畿餞送，鄉里榮之。

translations.literal: When he was about to go to his post the imperial carriage came to the near suburbs to see him off and feast him; his home district was glorified.
translations.idiomatic: As he set out for his post the emperor's carriage came to the near suburbs to feast and send him off. His home district took it as glory.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，徵拜散騎常侍、中護軍，鼓吹如故。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was summoned and appointed Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Central Guard Commander, martial pipes and drums as before.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was recalled as scattered-cavalry regular attendant and central guard commander, keeping his pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 留異之反東陽，詔瑒督舟師進討。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi rebelled in Dongyang an edict ordered Yang to command the river fleet in advance to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi rebelled in Dongyang an edict put Yang in command of the river fleet to attack him.

sentences.zh: 異平，遷鎮右將軍，常侍、鼓吹並如故。

translations.literal: When Yi was pacified he was transferred to General Who Guards the Right, regular attendant and martial pipes and drums unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi was crushed he was made general who guards the right, retaining his attendant post and pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出為使持節、安東將軍、建安太守。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Pacifying-the-East General, and Administrator of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as bearer of the staff, pacifying-the-east general, and administrator of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 光大中，以公事免，尋起為通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Guangda era he was removed for public business; soon he was raised again as Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangda era (567) he was dismissed on official grounds, then soon restored as direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，以瑒功名素著，深委任焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, because Yang's achievement and fame had long been outstanding, he deeply entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Yang's record and fame were already great, and the emperor relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 太建四年，授都督荊信二州諸軍事、安西將軍、荊州刺史，出鎮公安。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taijian he was given command of military affairs in Jing and Xin provinces, made Pacifying-the-West General and Inspector of Jing, and went out to garrison Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 4 (572) he was made commander of Jing and Xin, pacifying-the-west general and inspector of Jing, and marched out to hold Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 瑒增脩城池，懷服邊遠，為鄰境所憚。

translations.literal: Yang further repaired the walls and moats, won over the distant borders, and was feared by neighboring territories.
translations.idiomatic: He strengthened walls and moats, won over distant peoples, and neighboring states feared him.

sentences.zh: 居職六年，又以事免，更為通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After six years in office he was again removed for an affair and made Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant once more.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in post he was dismissed again on official grounds and returned as direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 及吳明徹軍敗呂梁，授使持節、督緣江水陸諸軍事、鎮西將軍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When Wu Mingche's army was defeated at Lüliang he was given Bearer of the Staff and command of river and land forces along the frontier, made General Who Guards the West, and given one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Mingche was broken at Lüliang he was made bearer of the staff, commander of frontier river and land forces, general who guards the west, with a suite of pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 尋授散騎常侍、都督荊郢巴武湘五州諸軍事、郢州刺史，持節、將軍、鼓吹並如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was given Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and command of military affairs in the five provinces of Jing, Ying, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, and Inspector of Ying; staff, general, and martial pipes and drums were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of Jing, Ying, Ba, Wu, and Xiang, and inspector of Ying, keeping staff, rank, and pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 十二年，坐疆埸交通抵罪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was punished for trafficking at the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was punished for illicit dealings on the border.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，復除通直散騎常侍，兼起部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded he was again removed and made Direct Communication Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, concurrently Minister for Founding Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor succeeded he was again made direct-communication scattered-cavalry regular attendant and concurrent minister for founding works.

sentences.zh: 尋除中護軍，復爵邑，入為度支尚書，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made Central Guard Commander, his noble rank and fief restored; he entered office as Minister of Revenue and led the Footsoldiers Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made central guard commander with rank and fief restored, then minister of revenue and leader of the footsoldiers commandant.

sentences.zh: 俄加散騎常侍，遷侍中、祠部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was added Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and transferred to Palace Attendant and Minister of the Ancestral Temples.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was added scattered-cavalry regular attendant, then made palace attendant and minister of the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 後主頻幸其第，及著詩賦述勳德之美，展君臣之意焉。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor often visited his residence, and composed poems and rhapsodies describing the beauty of his achievements, displaying the affection between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor often visited his house and wrote poems and rhapsodies praising his merit, showing the warmth between throne and subject.

sentences.zh: 又為五兵尚書，領右軍將軍，〔六〕侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was again made Minister of the Five Arms and led the Right Army General, Editorial footnote marker 6. palace attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made minister of the five arms and leader of the right army general, [6] retaining his palace attendant post.

sentences.zh: 以年老累乞骸骨，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Because of old age he repeatedly begged to retire on account of infirmity; gracious edicts would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Age wore on him and he repeatedly asked leave to retire; gracious edicts refused.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年卒官，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he died in office, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 1 (587) he died in office, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 後主臨哭盡哀，贈護軍將軍，侍中如故，給鼓吹一部，朝服一具，衣一襲，喪事量加資給，諡曰桓子。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor came in person to mourn and wept with utmost grief; posthumously he was given General Who Guards the Army, palace attendant as before, one set of martial pipes and drums, one set of court robes, one suit of garments; funeral rites were supplied in generous measure according to the occasion; his posthumous title was Huanzi.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor came in person to mourn with deepest grief. He was posthumously made general who guards the army, palace attendant as before, with pipes and drums, court robes, and a suit of garments; funeral costs were generously supplied; his posthumous title was Huanzi.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 7.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 7.

sentences.zh: 瑒事親以孝聞，於諸弟甚篤睦。

translations.literal: Yang served his parents with filial fame and was deeply affectionate toward his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was known for filial service to his parents and deep affection for his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 性通泰，有財物散之親友。

translations.literal: By nature he was open and easy; he had wealth and goods and gave them away to kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed by nature and gave his wealth freely to kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 其自居處，頗失於奢豪，庭院穿築，極林泉之致，歌鍾舞女，當世罕儔，賓客填門，軒蓋不絕。

translations.literal: In his own dwelling he rather failed in extravagance and pride; courtyards were dug through and built up to the utmost of forest and spring charm; singing bells and dancing girls were rare in the age; guests filled his gate and lofty carriages never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: His own household leaned toward luxury: courtyards were terraced into gardens to the limit of woodland and spring beauty; singing bells and dancing girls were seldom matched in the age; guests packed his gate and fine carriages never stopped coming.

sentences.zh: 及出鎮郢州，乃合十餘船為大舫，於中立亭池，植荷芰，每良辰美景，賓僚並集，泛長江而置酒，亦一時之勝賞焉。

translations.literal: When he went out to garrison Yingzhou he joined more than ten boats into a great barge; within it he set up a pavilion and pool and planted lotus and water chestnuts; on every fine day of good scenery officials and guests all gathered, set wine while drifting on the long river—it was also a splendor of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When he held Yingzhou he lashed more than ten boats into a great barge with a pavilion and pool inside and lotus planted about it. On fair days he gathered guests and officers, floated the long Yangzi with wine set out—a wonder of the age.

sentences.zh: 常於山齋設講肆，集玄儒之士，冬夏資奉，為學者所稱。

translations.literal: He often set up a lecture hall in his mountain studio, gathered scholars of the profound learning, and supported them winter and summer; scholars praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He often held a lecture hall in his mountain retreat, gathered learned men, and supported them winter and summer; scholars praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 而處己率易，不以名位驕物。

translations.literal: Yet in his own conduct he was easy and direct and did not treat others with arrogance because of name and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his own bearing he was plain and never looked down on others because of rank.

sentences.zh: 時興皇寺朗法師該通釋典，〔八〕瑒每造講筵，時有抗論，法侶莫不傾心。

translations.literal: At that time Master Lang of Xinghuang Temple had thoroughly mastered the Buddhist canon, Editorial footnote marker 8. and whenever Yang came to the lecture seat there was debate; the community of the Law all turned their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Master Lang of Xinghuang Temple had mastered the Buddhist canon. [8] Whenever Yang came to the lecture hall they argued points, and the monastic community hung on his words.

sentences.zh: 又巧思過人，為起部尚書，軍國器械，多所創立。

translations.literal: He was also surpassing in ingenious thought; as Minister for Founding Works he created many of the army's and state's engines and gear.
translations.idiomatic: His ingenuity surpassed others. As minister for founding works he devised much of the army's and state's equipment.

sentences.zh: 有鑒識，男女婚姻，皆擇素貴。

translations.literal: He had discernment; in marriages for sons and daughters he always chose families of plain nobility.
translations.idiomatic: He had a keen eye; for his children's marriages he always chose families of quiet distinction.

sentences.zh: 及卒，尚書令江總為其志銘，後主又題銘後四十字，遣左民尚書蔡徵宣敕就宅鐫之。

translations.literal: When he died, Secretariat Director Jiang Zong composed his funerary inscription; the Last Emperor also inscribed forty characters after the inscription and sent Left Household Minister Cai Zheng with an edict to his residence to carve it.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Secretariat Director Jiang Zong wrote his epitaph. The Last Emperor added forty characters of his own and sent Left Household Minister Cai Zheng with an edict to carve them at Yang's house.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：「秋風動竹，煙水驚波。

translations.literal: The words read: "Autumn wind stirs bamboo; misty waters startle the waves.
translations.idiomatic: The text runs: "Autumn wind stirs the bamboo; misted waters startle the waves.

sentences.zh: 幾人樵徑，何處山阿？

translations.literal: How many men on the woodcutters' path—where is that mountain slope?
translations.idiomatic: How many men on the woodcutters' path—where is that mountain slope?

sentences.zh: 今時日月，宿昔綺羅。

translations.literal: The sun and moon of today—the brocade and gauze of nights past.
translations.idiomatic: Today's sun and moon—the brocade and gauze of nights gone by.

sentences.zh: 天長路遠，地久雲多。

translations.literal: Heaven long, the road far; earth enduring, clouds many.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is long and the road far; earth endures and clouds are many.

sentences.zh: 功臣未勒，此意如何？

translations.literal: Meritorious ministers not yet inscribed—what of this intent?
translations.idiomatic: Merit not yet carved in stone—what shall we make of this heart?

sentences.zh: 」時論以為榮。

translations.literal: " Men of the time held it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of the time took it as glory.

sentences.zh: 瑒二十一子，咸有父風。

translations.literal: Yang had twenty-one sons; all had their father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had twenty-one sons, each with his father's bearing.

sentences.zh: 世子讓，早卒。

translations.literal: The heir Rang died young.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Rang died young.

sentences.zh: 第二子訓，頗知名，歷臨湘令，直閤將軍、高唐太守。

translations.literal: The second son Xun was rather famed; he served in succession as magistrate of Linxiang, Direct-Gate General, and Administrator of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Xun won some fame as magistrate of Linxiang, direct-gate general, and administrator of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋。

translations.literal: When Chen perished he entered Sui.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered Sui service.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：在梁之季，寇賊寔繁，高祖建義杖旗，將寧區夏，裴忌早識攀附，每預戎麾，〔摧〕鋒卻敵，〔九〕立功者數矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In the last years of Liang, bandits and rebels were truly numerous; the Founder raised righteousness and bore the standard, about to bring peace to the realm; Pei Ji early recognized whom to follow and was always in the military entourage; [smash] the enemy's edge and drive them back, Editorial footnote marker 9. he achieved merit many times.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In Liang's last years rebels swarmed. The Founder raised the banner of righteousness to pacify the realm. Pei Ji saw early whom to follow and was ever in the field, [smashing] the enemy's van and driving them back [9] again and again.

sentences.zh: 孫瑒有文武幹略、見知時主，及行軍用兵，師司馬之法，至於戰勝攻取，屢著勳庸，加以好施接物，士咸慕向。

translations.literal: Sun Yang had civil and military capacity and plan, was known to the ruler of the age; in marching armies and using troops he followed the methods of the Marshal; as to defeating the enemy in battle and taking by assault, he repeatedly achieved merit and fame; moreover he loved giving and received people well—officers and men all admired and turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yang had civil and military talent and won his sovereign's trust. In command he followed the marshal's art; in battle he took cities and won repeated glory. He was generous and approachable, and soldiers admired him.

sentences.zh: 然性不循恆，頻以罪免，蓋亦陳湯之徒焉。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he did not keep to constancy and was repeatedly removed for crimes—he was perhaps of Chen Tang's kind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was not steady by nature and was often dismissed for fault—perhaps a man in Chen Tang's mold.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 〔二〕 父循道 「循」南史作「修」。

translations.literal: Father Xundao—"Xun" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Xiu."
translations.idiomatic: On "father Xundao": the Southern Dynasties history reads Xiu for Xun.

sentences.zh: 〔三〕 徵瑒為太府卿 「太府卿」南史作「少府卿」，通鑑陳武帝永定三年同。

translations.literal: Summoned Yang as Minister of the Grand Storehouse—"Minister of the Grand Storehouse" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Minister of the Lesser Storehouse"; the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wudi Yongding year 3, agrees.
translations.idiomatic: On "summoned Yang as minister of the grand storehouse": the Southern Dynasties history reads minister of the lesser storehouse; the Comprehensive Mirror, Chen Wudi Yongding year 3, agrees.

sentences.zh: 〔五〕 徵為散騎常侍中領軍 南史作「徵為侍中、領軍將軍」。

translations.literal: Summoned as Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant and Central Army Commander—the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "summoned as Palace Attendant and Army Commander."
translations.idiomatic: On "summoned as scattered cavalry regular attendant and central army commander": the Southern Dynasties history reads summoned as palace attendant and army commander.

sentences.zh: 〔六〕 領右軍將軍 「右」南史作「左」。

translations.literal: Concurrently Right Army General—"Right" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "Left."
translations.idiomatic: On "concurrently right army general": the Southern Dynasties history reads left for right.

sentences.zh: 〔七〕 諡曰桓子 張森楷校勘記云「子」字衍。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Huan-zi—Zhang Senkai's collation note says the character "zi" is redundant.
translations.idiomatic: On "posthumous title Huan-zi": Zhang Senkai's collation note holds that zi is superfluous.

sentences.zh: 今按：瑒初封定襄縣侯，太建十二年坐疆埸交通抵罪免，後主嗣位，又復侯爵，此作「 子」不合，張說是。

translations.literal: Present review: Yang was first enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang county; in Taijian year 12 he was stripped for dealings at the frontier; when Emperor Houzhu succeeded he regained the marquisate—writing "zi" here does not fit; Zhang is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Present review: Yang was first made marquis of Dingxiang; in Taijian year 12 he lost his title for frontier dealings; when Houzhu succeeded he regained the marquisate—so zi here is wrong; Zhang is right.

sentences.zh: 〔八〕 時興皇寺朗法師該通釋典 「朗法師」元龜八二一作「慧朗法師」。

translations.literal: At that time Master Lang of Xinghuang Monastery was thoroughly versed in the Buddhist canon—"Master Lang" in Yuan Gui 821 reads "Master Huilang."
translations.idiomatic: On "Master Lang of Xinghuang Monastery, thoroughly versed in the Buddhist canon": Yuan Gui 821 reads Master Huilang.

translations.literal: Collation note nine.
translations.idiomatic: Collation note nine.

translations.literal: (Tui)
translations.idiomatic: (Tui)

sentences.zh: 〔摧〕鋒卻敵 據北監本、汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: [Cui] the sharp point and repel the enemy—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[crush] the vanguard and repel the enemy": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
